correctness.rationale: For each balanced-sign coordinate every prefix sum of a permutation is bounded by p. Abel summation bounds each epoch increment by p times the first-to-last stepsize decrease and hence by a telescoping subsequence decrease. Interior prefixes are bounded by p times the first step, preserving the sign cell and proving the full sequence converges. In the exact quadratic witness, the sign cell holds for every iterate, the limit is >=1, and F derivative is x. The random two-row epoch increments are independent Rademacher times adjacent step differences, giving exactly variance sum delta squared; harmonic difference-square identity is pi squared over 6 minus twice log 2. Exact-rational and numerical checks are included but infinite statements follow from proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the quantitative every-permutation, every-monotone-vanishing-step trapping criterion and the explicit two-quadratic random-limit formula, not the already-known general possibility of vanilla signSGD nonconvergence. The original 2023 SignRR full text (Algorithm 1, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.4, appendices) gives a potentially nonvanishing upper-bound error but not this positive lower bound or all-path limit law. A 2023 SignSVRG full text explicitly mentions generic signSGD failure but studies a different variance-reduced/noisy update. No statement implying the quantified theorem appeared in the queried published records or accessible own claims; uncertain older equivalent lemmas remain a real risk.

value.rationale: A nonvanishing error term in an expected stationarity upper bound does not establish an actual convergent yet nonstationary trajectory. Here a structurally defined balanced-sign region forces finite total epoch drift for any monotone diminishing schedule and all shuffle orders. Smooth 1-strongly-convex components eliminate nonconvex/nonsmooth explanations; Robbins-Monro compliant steps rule out a stepsize summability artifact. The exact harmonic limit variance characterizes residual randomization and provides a concrete stress test for sign-only optimization.
